ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are two transistors connected in series, one above and one below, with the upper end connected to VDD; the gate of the upper transistor is biased by V1, and the gate of the lower transistor is biased by V2. VOUT is led out from the drain/series node between the two transistors. The source path of the lower transistor goes downward through resistor R1, then connects to the input source labeled VIN, and finally is grounded. Reasoning: The problem states that V1 and V2 are bias voltages, so they are not signal input terminals. The signal input VIN is applied to the source path of the lower transistor and enters the circuit through R1; the small-signal input impedance of this source/common-gate input is relatively low, so the input control quantity appears as current. The output terminal VOUT is located at the drain node, and the upper-and-lower stacked transistor structure provides a relatively high small-signal output impedance; high output impedance corresponds to the output quantity appearing as current. Therefore, classified by input and output impedances, this circuit is equivalent to a current-controlled current source.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown, where \(V_1\) and \(V_2\) are bias voltages, what type of source does the circuit behave as based on its input and output impedances?

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit structure from the image: the input port VIN feeds the lower transistor source path through R1, while the output port VOUT is at a transistor drain node; the gates are not signal inputs because V1 and V2 are DC bias voltages. Treat the lower source/input node as a current-sensing input, which has low small-signal input impedance due to the source/common-gate connection. Treat the drain-side output node, helped by the stacked transistor arrangement, as having high small-signal output impedance. Then apply the source-model classification table: low input impedance means the controlling variable is current, and high output impedance means the delivered variable is current. Therefore the circuit behaves as a current controlled current source.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: two biased MOS transistors are stacked vertically, with V1 and V2 connected only as gate bias nodes; the actual signal enters at the lower source-side terminal VIN through R1, and the output is taken as VOUT at the drain/intermediate node. Since the gates are fixed biases, variations of VIN mainly force a small-signal current into the source of the lower transistor. In common-gate operation this source current appears as drain/output current, while the stacked biased transistor arrangement keeps the output resistance large. Thus the controlling quantity is the input current and the generated quantity is the output current, so the circuit behaves as a current controlled current source.
